title: Five-Finger Sequence · Classic
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Five-Finger Sequence · Classic with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: A partner selects three different fingers on one hand. The partner points to them in order; the lead repeats the sequence. The lead points to the same fingers in the same order. Each player takes two turns. Give the lead one point for each successful turn. Highest score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Five-Finger Sequence, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The lead points to the same fingers in the same order.
recall.why: The lead points to the same fingers in the same order.
